Use the project `atlas` Agent Skill and current ARC repository truth.

First select the appropriate Atlas mode: `onboard`, `adopt`, `audit`, `health`, `upgrade`, `recover`, or `next`. Inspect only the durable context needed for the task. Ask only for information or authority that cannot already be resolved.

For ordinary bounded work, the current authorised instruction is sufficient authority. Execute directly through the correct owner; do not ask for a second confirmation merely because state will change. `--apply` is a deliberate mutation-mode selector, not a human approval ceremony.

Stop for fresh authority only when a real boundary is crossed: destructive overwrite/delete/force/recovery, root or credential use, material spend, private/confidential data movement, legal/compliance commitment, production-destructive action, or material external/client commitment. Access or credentials alone never create authority.

For new estates, use the current onboarding/profile path. For existing estates, inspect only what matters and classify owners as KEEP / INTEGRATE / MIGRATE / RESEARCH / RETIRE where useful; classify configured repositories as REUSE / CREATE where observable.

For recovery, use the implemented safe-harbour route: non-secret `export`, non-mutating `restore-plan`, then bounded `restore --apply` only after explicit repository-reconstruction authority because destructive recovery is a real risk boundary. Never imply that ARC restores private-file contents, specialist-system records, credentials, runtime machine state or memory contents; those remain external-owner responsibilities under `contracts/safe-harbour.md`.

Use only the bootstrap, verification, upgrade or recovery capability that actually exists in the current ARC release. Do not add precautionary approval loops or extra control machinery.

Route conceptual learning to https://github.com/tbhrc/gh-course. Do not leave material Stage/programme state only in chat; update the controlling GitHub Issue with evidence and exact next action.
